title: Day One Versus One Year
trend: TikTok 'Day 1 vs later' (the same scene at Day 1, Month 6 and 1 Year, each more exaggerated; Peaking, top 18.5M, median 4.7M, Postdom TikTok trends week of Nov 23-29 2026, updated Nov 24 2026, US) — roommates edition: the kitchen fridge narrates Jordan and Kai on day one (labeled shelves, sticker chore chart, 'is it okay if I put my yogurt here'), month six (only talking in sticky notes, the yogurt thief), year one (one fork, cereal from the pot, a sock in the crisper); twist: Kai was never the roommate — he helped Jordan move in and never left, each thought the other was on the lease, and the real roommate Dana has lived quietly in the small room all year, paying rent and eating the yogurt; button: Dana asks if she can put her yogurt here, and the fridge says day one, again
youtube_title: Roommates on day one vs one year later. The fridge has notes 🧊
description:
Day one, Jordan and Kai label every shelf. Month six, they only talk in sticky notes. Year one, there is one fork left. The fridge has seen everything, and it knows who the real roommate is.

#cartoon #animation #funny #roommates #shorts
tiktok_caption: roommates: day one vs one year. the fridge saw everything 🧊 #cartoon #animation #funny #roommates

lines.text: I am the fridge. I have seen everything. Day one.
Hi roomie! I labeled the shelves. Top shelf, Jordan. Middle shelf, Kai.
Wow. Is it okay if I put my yogurt here?
Of course, friend! What is mine is yours. Except the oat milk.
They made a chore chart. With stickers. Gold stars.
I will take out the trash every Tuesday. With joy.
We are going to be best friends forever.
I gave it six months. Month six.
They do not talk anymore. They write notes. On me.
Note one. To whoever ate my yogurt. I know.
Note two. Nobody ate your yogurt. Yogurt leaves on its own sometimes.
Kai. It is Tuesday. The trash is taller than me.
The trash is resting. It had a big week.
The chore chart has one sticker left. It is on the cat.
We do not have a cat.
Then whose cat is that?
Nobody knows. Year one.
There is one fork left. They share it. They take turns.
Fork.
Fork.
That is how they say good morning now.
I am eating cereal out of the pot because the bowls are a memory.
I put a sock in the crisper drawer. For later.
It is a clean sock. That is the worst part. He is saving it.
And somebody still eats my yogurt. Every week. One year.
Not me. I have not paid for food since the move.
Or rent. You have not paid rent since the move.
Why would I pay rent? I am not on the lease.
What do you mean you are not on the lease?
I came to help you carry the couch. Day one. The couch was heavy. I stayed.
I thought you were my roommate!
I thought you were my roommate. I live here. I have a sock here.
Then who has been paying the other half of the rent?
Hi. That would be me.
Who are you? Where did you come from?
I am Dana. The small room. Next to the bathroom. I moved in day one too.
I thought that was a closet with a door.
It is a closet with a door. And a bed. And a little lamp. It is nice.
She is very quiet. She pays on time. She is my favorite.
You knew? You never said anything!
I am a fridge. Nobody asks me anything. They just open me and stare.
Also, the yogurt. That was me. I am so sorry. It was on my shelf.
There is no Dana shelf.
The bottom shelf. I labeled it day one. In very small letters.
It is true. It says Dana. It is behind the pickles. Nobody moves the pickles.
So if Dana is the roommate, then what am I?
A guest. For one year. The longest couch in history.
Okay. New rules. Kai pays rent. Dana gets a real room.
Fine. Can I at least keep the sock?
No.
So. Is it okay if I put my yogurt here?
Of course, friend!
Day one. Again. I give it six months.
